newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent flat amid Europe refinery disruption.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent flat amid Europe refinery disruption.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were almost unchanged on Monday in thin volumes as traders awaited fresh news on Iraq oil exports.
September Brent crude oil opened five cents down at $18.90 a barrel but climbed back to $18.97 by 0945 GMT. August gas oil opened $1.25 up at $172.75 a tonne.
Dealers said a little of gas oil's strength was a continued reaction to news on Friday of technical problems with catalytic cracking units at three refineries in Europe.
Brokers at the IPE said they had seen no fresh market-moving news from Iraq.
Baghdad is waiting to restart oil exports under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations. Exports have been delayed by wrangling over Iraq's aid distribution plan.
A U.N. spokesman said last week he expected approval of the aid distribution plan early this week.

Technical analysts said Brent faced resistance first at the psychologically important $19.00 level, and then at Thursday'S high of $19.09. Trendline support lay at $18.57 on Monday, they said. But overbought signals suggested some room for downwards movement, they added.

Gas oil faces resistance at the top of a previous chart gap from $172.7 to $173.50 a tonne, and the contract briefly bumped up against this latter number at the market open on Monday before falling back.

MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing the Market Profile technique, said: "everything except Brent (is) looking decidedly more negative than last week. We trade with light volumes as news from Iraq is imminent and this could disrupt the technical picture."
